# Psalm 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Of-David, when-he-changed his-behavior before Abimelech, who-drove-him-out, and-he-went-away.

**2** I-will-bless YHWH at-every time; continually His-praise [is] in-my-mouth.

**3** In-YHWH my-soul boasts; the-humble hear and-are-glad.

**4** Magnify YHWH with-me, and-let-us-exalt His-name together.

**5** I-sought YHWH, and-He-answered-me, and-from-all my-terrors He-delivered-me.

**6** They-looked to-Him and-were-radiant, and-their-faces shall-never be-ashamed.

**7** This poor-man called, and-YHWH heard, and-from-all his-distresses He-saved-him.

**8** The-angel of-YHWH encamps around those-who-fear-Him, and-delivers-them.

**9** Taste and-see that YHWH [is] good; blessed [is] the-man [who] takes-refuge in-Him.

**10** Fear YHWH, His-holy-ones, for there-is-no lack for-those-who-fear-Him.

**11** Young-lions lack and-hunger, but-those-seeking YHWH shall-not lack any good.

**12** Come, children, listen to-me; the-fear of-YHWH I-will-teach-you.

**13** Who [is] the-man who-desires life, loving days to-see good?

**14** Keep your-tongue from-evil, and-your-lips from-speaking deceit.

**15** Turn from-evil and-do good; seek peace and-pursue-it.

**16** The-eyes of-YHWH [are] toward the-righteous, and-His-ears [are] toward their-cry.

**17** The-face of-YHWH [is] against-those-doing evil, to-cut-off from-the-earth their-memory.

**18** [The righteous] cry-out, and-YHWH hears, and-from-all their-distresses He-delivers-them.

**19** Near [is] YHWH to-the-brokenhearted, and-the-crushed in-spirit He-saves.

**20** Many [are] the-afflictions of-the-righteous, but-from-all-of-them YHWH delivers-him.

**21** He-keeps all his-bones; not one of-them is-broken.

**22** Evil slays the-wicked, and-those-hating the-righteous shall-be-condemned.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **34:1**: An acrostic psalm. The superscription says 'Abimelech,' but 1 Samuel 21 calls the Philistine king 'Achish' — Abimelech may be a throne name.

- **34:21**: 'Not one of them is broken' — John 19:36 applies this to Jesus on the cross, whose bones were not broken, unlike the two criminals.

— EMET
